context: The gate of a small Kobe apartment building, morning. A new resident (Ren) has just brought down his recycling and Mrs. Mori is, predictably, already there.
purpose: neighbourhood orientation + gossip + welcome — Kansai community contact

lines.speaker: mrs_mori_neighbor
lines.jp: あ、新しい人やんね？おはようさん。
lines.en: Oh — you're the new one, aren't you? Mornin'.
lines.style: Bright, instantly familiar. Kansai cadence. The 「おはようさん」 is half-greeting, half-claim of jurisdiction.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: おはようございます。先週、引っ越してきました。
lines.en: Good morning. I moved in last week.
lines.style: Polite, slightly startled by the warmth. Tokyo formality meeting Kansai warmth.

lines.speaker: mrs_mori_neighbor
lines.jp: そうそうそう。ゴミの日、わかってる？火曜と金曜やからね。
lines.en: Yeah yeah yeah — you know the garbage days? Tuesdays and Fridays, okay?
lines.style: Three quick agreement-syllables, then straight into useful intel. The information has been waiting.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、本当にありがとうございます。
lines.style: A small bow inside the voice. Adjusting his pace slightly upward to match hers.

lines.speaker: mrs_mori_neighbor
lines.jp: あと、上の階の人、夜ちょっとうるさい時あるけど、いい人やから大丈夫。
lines.en: Oh — the upstairs folks can be a bit loud at night sometimes, but they're good people, so it's fine.
lines.style: The intel keeps coming. Pre-empts a worry he hasn't had yet. Affectionate about the loud upstairs.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.style: Bemused — accepting that this is now his life. Small smile in the voice.

lines.speaker: mrs_mori_neighbor
lines.jp: なんかあったら、いつでも来てな。時間あるから、私。
lines.en: If anything comes up — come round any time, dear. I've got nothing but time.
lines.style: Warm, open. The 「時間あるから、私」 is a brag and a gift at once.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本当に、ありがとうございます。
lines.style: Sincere, lands a tiny bit warmer than the first thank-you. He's on her side of the gate now.
